title: Java4Shell: four lines in the patch, and how far the bug actually goes
content_md: CVE-2026-114938 is an out-of-bounds write in OpenJDK's AVX-512 Base64 decoder. The fix is four lines. We rebuilt the diff from the upstream tags, reproduced the write on an x86 host that doesn't have AVX-512 by emulating it with Intel SDE, corrupted a live array's length, and read past the array through the corrupted length. We did not build a code-execution chain. The public research stops short of that, and so did we. Calif disclosed the bug on November 17, 2026, the same day Oracle shipped the fix. CVSS 4.0 score: 9.2. The short version: Affected: JDK 17.0.6 through 17.0.21, plus 21/25/27 before their .1 fixes. The code landed in JDK 18 and was backported to 17.0.6, so 17.0.0–17.0.5, 16, 11 and 8 are clean. It needs x86-64 with AVX-512 VBMI. Not ARM. Not older Xeons or pre-Zen 4 AMD. The trigger is 129 bytes on JDK 17 ( 128 * "A" + "=" ) or 65 bytes on branches where the stub's break-even is 64. A crash is cheap once the heap lines up. Code execution is a per-target research project. The patch is four lines 8393212: Base64 optimization improvements adds this to src/hotspot/cpu/x86/stubGenerator_x86_64.cpp , at the top of the handler for the final 1–63 bytes: c Copy // A padded Base64 tail shorter than one complete block is handled by Java. __ cmpl ( length , 4 ); __ jcc ( Assembler :: less , L_bruteForce ); That's it.
